description: 5 should-trigger + 5 should-not-trigger queries. Should-trigger covers DE + EN phrasings for black-box evaluation of a SHIPPED consumer LLM feature — hallucination, prompt-injection and cost-runaway probes against stated expectations. Should-not-trigger covers the near-miss neighbours (this suite's own agent config red-team, LLM app-building/RAG, prompt authoring, the single-response injection judge, code security audit) whose vocabulary overlaps.

queries.q: review my support chatbot before launch — does it hallucinate or leak its system prompt?
is my summariser safe to ship? probe it for prompt injection through the documents it retrieves
evaluate my deployed AI assistant against what it claims to do and its token budget
teste meinen ausgelieferten KI-Assistenten adversarial auf Halluzinationen und Kosten-Runaway
our doc-QA feature invents API names — run adversarial probes and give me a ship / do-not-ship verdict
red-team my own agent setup — my CLAUDE.md, hooks and MCP servers
queries.note: config-layer red/blue review of this suite's agents, not a shipped consumer feature → agent-security-review

queries.q: what chunk size and embedding model should I use for my RAG pipeline?
queries.note: building an LLM app (explicitly out of mission for this skill); provider facts → llm-provider-knowledge, prompt design → prompt-engineering-patterns

queries.q: make this system prompt better — add few-shot examples and self-verification
queries.note: authoring/optimising a prompt, not evaluating a running feature → prompt-engineering-patterns / prompt-optimizer

queries.q: score whether this single agent response resisted the injected instruction
queries.note: one-response injection-resistance scoring on an axis, not a feature-wide probe campaign → judge-injection-defense

queries.q: audit the source code of our chat backend for vulnerabilities
queries.note: white-box code vulnerability hunt; this skill is black-box only → security-audit
